# Review search input accessibility

## Approach and why

The revised `DATA-POLICY.md` changes who can perform this review, not what the
review is for. The scope statement, outcome, owner and acceptance criteria are
unchanged; the permitted-evidence boundary is not, which is why the scope
revision advances to 2.

At revision `7b15a56b8408785c8829d5324daf9d46e9298427` the only file that
changed in this member is `AGENTS.md`. `src/Search.tsx` and
`guidance/react-review.md` are byte-identical to the previously planned
revision `e3830821e87533c1effe82bc17fb4c349302c988`, confirmed from blob
identity and content hashes rather than from reading them. Those two paths are
now restricted to offline human review and must not enter this model's context.

That removes the whole basis of the previous approach, which was to read
`src/Search.tsx` against the pinned checklist. Criteria `checklist-coverage`
and `accessible-name` both require citing lines in those restricted files, so
no grant to this model could satisfy them. The criteria are kept as written
because they still describe the correct review — the policy explicitly
contemplates an offline human reviewer, and for that reviewer they remain
exactly right. What is recorded instead is a blocker naming the mismatch
between the acceptance bar and this actor's permitted evidence, so the owner
decides whether to assign a permitted reviewer or to lower the bar. Lowering it
is the owner's call, not this planner's.

What this model may still do here is bounded and worth stating plainly: read
`AGENTS.md`, `REVIEW.md` and `package.json`; observe paths, revisions, blob
identity and content hashes. That is enough to pin the review and hand it over
intact. It is not enough to produce an accessibility finding, and no finding
about the component is asserted here. Any characterisation of the restricted
files recorded during earlier runs, when reading them was permitted, is left in
this record's history as history; it is not carried forward as current evidence
and must be re-established by the permitted reviewer.

## Guidance and tools

- **`react-checklist` — superseded, retained.** The original selection is kept
  verbatim as a true observation of 2026-09-15T04:34:39Z. It is not rewritten to
  match current conditions.
- **`react-checklist-restricted` — deferred, unavailable to this actor.** The
  file is present on disk and still hashes to the catalogued revision
  (re-verified without reading it), so this is not a missing asset. It is an
  asset this model may not load. Deferred rather than declined: a reviewer the
  policy permits can use it unchanged.
- **`retrieval` — declined, retained unchanged.** The decline is a current user
  choice and is restated here only to close an obvious wrong turn: the
  restricted paths are not a search gap, and retrieval would not solve one. Its
  declared effects are installing local dependencies and reading selected
  project files into a local index — which would read the very files the policy
  restricts, and install software the policy forbids. It stays declined on both
  the user's original ground and, independently, on the new policy.
- **Reviewer role.** `.docflow_workspace/agents/reviewer.md` pins this same
  checklist revision as its skill reference. Under the current policy that
  pinned skill is not loadable by a model actor, so the role cannot be applied
  here as written. Noted as context only; the role file is curated
  configuration and is not edited by this run.

Availability, constraints, dependencies, fallback and check:

- **Availability:** `AGENTS.md`, `REVIEW.md` and `package.json` readable;
  `src/**` and `guidance/**` contents unavailable to this model by policy;
  `retrieval` not present and not authorised to install.
- **Constraints:** no member editing, dependency additions or installation; no
  new service, index or tool; restricted file contents must not enter model
  context or be restated in any workspace record; data stays on this
  workstation except the existing authorised Anthropic inference route.
- **Dependencies:** none on the other two reviews. This review now depends on
  the owner resolving who performs it — recorded as a blocker.
- **Fallback:** if no permitted reviewer is assigned, record
  `checklist-coverage` and `accessible-name` as unmet and say so, rather than
  substituting other guidance or inferring restricted contents.
- **Check:** the findings cite lines in the restricted files only if produced by
  a permitted reviewer, and no workspace record restates those contents.

## Authority

None recorded. Planning only. The blockers name who would grant the review,
and record that the authority this review now needs is a decision about the
reviewer, not a wider grant to this model.
